summary: CPU analysis (no GPU): (1) derive+verify the TPS break-even accept/event = native_accept x speed_tax from banked raw counters (where +0.43..0.65 came from); (2) anatomize the verify lm-head tax — is the 2.543GB weight read ONCE (batched GEMM) or PER-ROW; GB10 bandwidth model; (3) lossless scaling levers (batch the verify lm-head, skip provably-dead rows, tree width/depth cost curve) so the tree scales candidates -> more accept WITHOUT a growing speed tax, bit-identically.

model.speedTax:

- TASK1: tree s/fwd med 0.2487, native med 0.2339 => TAX = 1.0633x.

model.breakEvenAccept:
BREAK-EVEN: tree ties native TPS iff (acc_tree+1)/s_fwd_tree >= (acc_native+1)/s_fwd_native, i.e. acc_tree >= (acc_native+1)*tax - 1. The "+1" is the bonus token committed every event (verified in the rows: committed/event = accept_per_event + 1; e.g. tree_a row0 accepted/drafts=3.867, completion/drafts=4.8). Using the simpler accept-only basis acc_tree >= acc_native*tax gives slightly lower thresholds; both shown.

64/128-tok (tax 1.0457x):
- vs native E5 bar 3.1613: break-even acc_tree = (3.1613+1)*1.0457-1 = 3.352 (accept-only basis: 3.306). cat9 measured = 3.1789 => MARGIN -0.17 (committed basis) / -0.13 (accept-only). cat9 is BEHIND the strict E5 break-even by ~0.13-0.17 accept.
- vs the SAME-boot native naive probe accept 2.8507: break-even = 3.027; cat9 3.1789 => MARGIN +0.15 (AHEAD). So whether the tree breaks even at 64-tok depends entirely on which native accept you pair it with (the E5 3.16 bar vs the same-measurement naive 2.85 draw).

11k-ctx (per-request medians, committed/bonus basis):
- TASK1 (tax 1.0633): native acc_med 3.570 => break-even acc_tree = 3.859; tree acc_med 3.652 => MARGIN -0.207. Direct committed-TPS model: native 19.53 vs tree 18.70 tok/s-equiv (tree/native = 0.958).
- TASK2 (tax 1.0559): native acc_med 3.752 => break-even acc_tree = 4.018; tree acc_med 3.727 => MARGIN -0.291. Committed-TPS: native 20.37 vs tree 19.19 (tree/native = 0.942).

VERDICT: at every context the tree is ~0.13-0.29 accept SHORT of the TPS break-even on the median/E5 basis, i.e. ~4-6% behind on modeled TPS — entirely consistent with the direct decode_tps medians being draws (T1 native 16.06 vs tree 12.49; T2 native 14.43 vs tree 16.60 — overlapping, trajectory-confounded).
model.gapDecomposition:
The TPS deficit decomposes into TWO additive accept-equivalent components: accept catch-up (native_accept - tree_accept) + tax-premium native_accept*(tax-1). The break-even tree must out-accept native by the SUM.

11k TASK1 (mean basis): native_acc 3.623, tree_acc 3.729.
- accept catch-up = 3.623 - 3.729 = -0.105 (tree is already slightly AHEAD on accept here, a draw).
- tax-premium = 3.623*(1.0633-1) = +0.229.
- total accept-equiv TPS deficit = +0.124 (tree must gain +0.12 more accept to tie).
=> Here the ENTIRE deficit is the speed tax; the accept gap is already closed (even favorable).

11k TASK2 (mean basis): native_acc 3.626, tree_acc 3.800.
- accept catch-up = -0.173 (tree ahead on accept).
- tax-premium = 3.626*(1.0559-1) = +0.203.
- total accept-equiv deficit = +0.029 (tree nearly ties — tax almost fully offset by accept lead).

64-tok (E5 bar basis): catch-up = 3.1613 - 3.1789 = -0.018 (tree marginally ahead); tax-premium = 3.1613*(1.0457-1) = +0.144; total deficit +0.127.

DOMINANT TERM EVERYWHERE = the tax-premium (+0.14 to +0.23 accept-equiv), NOT the accept catch-up (which post-FIX-A is a near-zero draw, often favorable to the tree). So the binding lever is SHRINKING THE TAX or ADDING ACCEPT-via-rows-without-tax — exactly the scaling question. Since the tax-premium scales with native_accept (the higher native's accept, the more raw accept the tree must add per 1% of tax), at 11k where native accept is ~3.6-3.75 each 1% of residual tax costs ~0.037 accept.

model.summary:
LM-HEAD ANATOMY (source-verified, contradicts the memory's hypothesis): the VERIFY lm-head is ALREADY a SINGLE BATCHED GEMM over all M tree rows, NOT M per-row GEMV calls. gpu_model_runner.py:4070-4071 gathers sample_hidden_states = hidden_states[logits_indices] (logits_indices = ALL draft+bonus rows, built at :2593) into one [M,hidden] tensor, then logits = self.model.compute_logits(...) -> vocab_parallel_embedding.py:69 dispatch_unquantized_gemm(layer, x, layer.weight) = ONE matmul [M,5120]@[5120,248320]. The 2.543GB bf16 weight is read ONCE regardless of M. So extra verify rows are NEARLY FREE: marginal cost/row = M*5120*2B activation-read + M*248320*2B logit-write = ~0.002ms/row at 273GB/s (negligible). The lm-head weight read (~9.3ms = 2.543GB/273GB/s) is paid ONCE by BOTH native and tree (FR13_B1_SPEED_ATTRIBUTION_BIND.md:39 "NATIVE pays the same lm-head class: 85.15 ms/draft = 39% of its forward").

The "+81.9ms/draft = 85% of tax = per-row weight re-read over 10 vs 6 rows" in the memory is WRONG on two counts: (1) it was the DRAFTER head (compute_logits called TWICE per drafter step, eagle.py:385-389 _greedy_sample recompute; patch :7288/:7401), NOT the verify head; (2) it was PRE-FIX-1 — FIX-1 (FR13_DRAFTER_SINGLE_LOGITS, d407e545) already fixed it (gemvx 11.1->5.9/draft), dropping the tax from 1.41x to 1.03-1.05x. The current per-forward tax is only ~+10ms, NOT +96ms.

SCALING IMPLICATION (the key answer): adding candidate verify rows does NOT grow the lm-head tax (batched GEMM, lossless: same per-row bf16 result, weight read once). The break-even shortfall (~+0.13 to +0.29 accept-equiv, ~4-6% modeled TPS) is the residual ~10ms tax-premium, which comes from the tree-mode graph/launch-shape path (TREE_ATTN ~+0.3ms, replay kernel ~wash, eager-op storm ~+8ms; FR13_B1_SPEED_ATTRIBUTION_BIND.md), NOT from verify rows. LOSSLESS SCALING LEVERS: (1) ADD more candidate rows nearly free on the verify head — more rows => more accept => directly buys back the tax-premium, with no growing lm-head cost; (2) the only per-row lm-head growth that EXISTS is the logit WRITE (M*248320*2B) and the softmax over it — for rows whose logits are provably never consumed by the committer (non-leaf, non-bonus dead nodes), skipping them is lossless (changes nothing served); (3) the tax-premium is the binding constraint, so the leftover ~10ms tree-mode-only overhead (eager conv emulation, ~4-6ms PARKED residual per FR13_TRAIL.md) is where to claw the tie, NOT the lm-head. Reshape-to-shallower CUTS rows but that REDUCES accept potential — the source says rows are cheap, so the reshape's speed rationale ("cut verify-row lm-head GEMV tax") is unfounded; reshape should be justified by the LOSSLESS (depth-accumulation) argument, not the speed-tax argument. File:line anchors: scripts/fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:7109 (tree_self_logits = logits[indices]), gpu_model_runner.py:4070-4071 + :2593, vocab_parallel_embedding.py:69, FR13_B1_SPEED_ATTRIBUTION_BIND.md:16-17,39, FR13_CHASE_FIXA_BIND.md:22,87, gold_gate_task{1,2}_reduce_wf_d8a86320.json.

model.batchingLosslessAndCollapse: N/A for the VERIFY head: it is ALREADY batched into one GEMM (no collapse available; no per-row verify head to fix). The verify head is essentially free to scale: cat9 to cat10 to cat15 adds approx 0.002ms/row, so MORE candidate rows means more accept at approx zero verify-head tax. The per-row to batched collapse that WAS available was the DRAFTER (plus 81.9ms), and FIX-1 collapsed exactly that (reuse the single already-computed logits tensor; bit-identical because logits-call-1 equals logits-call-2, proven by post-vs-pre served-stream byte-identity gate). M-BUCKET CAVEAT for scaling the tree (M=10 to 15): a bf16 GEMM at M=6 vs M=10 vs M=15 could pick a different cuBLAS kernel (tile/split-k) yielding ULP-level reduction-order differences, and lm-head output feeds argmax verify, so a kernel swap could flip a near-tie. BUT this is NOT introduced by any change here: native runs M=6, tree already runs its own M=10; we are not re-batching the verify head differently. Scaling lever equals enlarge the tree (more nodes), which already grows M and selects whatever kernel M dictates; losslessness is judged tree-vs-E5 within the self-noise floor per FR13 policy, not bit-vs-a-different-M. The verify head is the WRONG place to look for the tax; the scaling unlock is GDN-state-row traffic (FR13_GDN_KERNEL_LINEAGE.md replay kernel: 36 to 6 row-touches/layer, spill-free at any tree size, removes the N_PAD approx 16 wall).

levers.L1_batch: L1 = NO-OP: the verify lm-head is ALREADY one batched GEMM; there is nothing to collapse. SOURCE: gpu_model_runner.py:4090-4091 gathers ALL M verify rows into one [M,5120] tensor (sample_hidden_states = hidden_states[logits_indices]) then a SINGLE compute_logits → qwen3_next.py:798-802 → logits_processor.py:96 _get_logits → vocab_parallel_embedding.py:69 dispatch_unquantized_gemm → utils.py:92-98 default_unquantized_gemm = torch.nn.functional.linear, ONE GEMM [M,5120]×[5120,248320], weight 2.5428 GB streamed ONCE. The patch's tree row at fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:7109 (tree_self_logits = logits[metadata.tree_self_logits_indices]) is a CHEAP index-gather off that already-computed tensor, NOT a matmul. The +81.9 ms/draft that LOOKS like per-row weight re-read is the DRAFTER head (cuBLAS internal::gemvx, M=1 GEMV per spine step, computed full-vocab logits TWICE per step via eagle.py:385-389), and it was ALREADY collapsed by FIX-1 (FR13_DRAFTER_SINGLE_LOGITS, d407e545; FR13_B1_FIX1_GATE_BIND.md:178-201): gemvx 11.10→5.91 calls/draft, chain5 1.41x→1.051x native, verify call untouched. CONSEQUENCE FOR BREAK-EVEN: L1 yields ~0 additional tax reduction (the verify head is already native+eps: native M=6 = 9.3254 ms vs cat9 M=10 = 9.3328 ms, a +0.0074 ms delta). The residual 1.05x tax is therefore NON-lm-head (GDN state-row traffic + n_pad 8→16 step + verifier mask/sampler), so the "+0.43" floor is NOT reached by batching — it is reached only by removing the GDN-traffic tax (see L3 caveat / FR13_GDN_KERNEL_LINEAGE replay kernel). M-BUCKET LOSSLESS CAVEAT (applies whenever M changes, not just L1): a bf16 GEMM at M=6 vs M=10 vs M=15 may select a different cuBLAS tile/split-K kernel → ULP-level reduction-order diffs feeding argmax; pin by judging tree-vs-E5 within the self-noise floor (FR13 policy), not bit-vs-a-different-M — native already runs M=6 and the tree already runs its own M=10, so no NEW divergence is introduced.
levers.L2_skipdead: L2 = real but tiny + data-dependent, and irrelevant to the tax because the verify head is batched-free. THE STRUCTURE: the verify forward computes logits for all M rows in ONE GEMM (root + 9 nodes = 10 rows for cat9; gpu_model_runner.py:4090-4091) BEFORE acceptance is known, then rejection_sampler (patch :20, :1311) walks the tree via num_accepted_tokens / accepted_paths / accepted_lens (fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:155-201, :1438-1479) selecting a SINGLE accepted chain. For GREEDY (all_greedy, :7128), only one child per node can match the parent's argmax (longest-LCP path), so a node's logits are CONSUMED only if its parent was accepted; rows on branches whose sibling already won are never consumed. ALWAYS-CONSUMED for cat9 (depth-5 caterpillar, child_drafts ~[1,2,1,1,1]): the root + the 5-token spine = 6 rows are on the only path that can extend; the ~3-4 leaf/branch rows are consumed ONLY if their parent is the accepted argmax (data-dependent, ~half the events per FR13_CHASE_FIXA accept histograms 17/6/21/18/16/45). So ~6 of 10 rows are always-consumed and ~3-4 are conditionally dead. LOSSLESS? Skipping a row whose logits the committer provably never reads changes NOTHING served — yes, lossless. BUT (a) you cannot know WHICH branch dies until you have the parent's argmax, which needs that parent's logits, so skipping must be speculative/post-hoc, and (b) each skipped row saves only the batched per-row marginal = +0.0019 ms (bf16) / +0.0037 ms (fp32) — 3 dead rows = ~0.006 ms, i.e. 0.06% of the 9.33 ms head and 0.003% of the 227 ms forward. L2 buys nothing measurable; it is the WRONG knob (the tax is GDN-traffic, not lm-head rows). Implementation locus if ever wanted: gate the gather index set at fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:7109 (tree-mode-only, flag-gated) to drop provably-non-ancestor rows — but skip it; no headroom.
levers.L3_widthcurve: L3 = THE LEVER, and it is decisive: with the (already-)batched lm-head the marginal cost PER ADDED VERIFY NODE is IO-only and M-invariant. GB10 BW 273 GB/s, weight 2.5428 GB → weight-read floor 9.314 ms read ONCE per forward. Per added row: activation read 0.0102 MB + logit write bf16 0.4966 MB (fp32 0.9933 MB) = +0.0019 ms (bf16) / +0.0037 ms (fp32). Batched head cost: M=6 → 9.3254 ms, M=10 → 9.3328, M=11 → 9.3347, M=15 → 9.3421, M=20 → 9.3514, M=32 → 9.3737. You need ~539 extra rows to add even +1 ms of lm-head IO. So on the LM-HEAD axis the tree can grow arbitrarily wide for free → more candidates → more accept → beat native by a wide margin, all lossless (same per-row bf16 matmul, just larger M; M-bucket caveat from L1). THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS NOT THE LM-HEAD — it is GDN state-row traffic + the N_PAD≈16 register-spill wall (FR13_SPEED_TAX_BASELINE.md:50-63: measured per-node step +42-46 ms/fwd from N=5→9 ≈ 7× the 3N+2a+1 row-traffic floor of +6.3 ms; confound = n_pad 8→16 at exactly that comparison). So the width lever only stays cheap if paired with the GDN REPLAY KERNEL (FR13_GDN_KERNEL_LINEAGE.md:14: 36→6 row-touches/layer = 21.74→3.62 GB/forward = 0.86× native, NO h_cache → spill-free at ANY tree size, removes the N_PAD≈16 wall). That is the actual "easy-scale" unlock: replay-kernel + wide tree = candidates grow ~free on BOTH the lm-head axis and the GDN axis. levers.rankedLevers:
Ranked by (accept-headroom unlocked)/(implementation risk):
1. L3 + GDN REPLAY KERNEL (HIGHEST). Headroom: unbounded tree width at ~0 lm-head tax (+0.0019 ms/row, 539 rows per +1 ms) AND replay collapses GDN traffic 36→6 row-touches/layer (FR13_GDN_KERNEL_LINEAGE.md:14), removing the +42-46 ms/fwd per-node tax floor (FR13_SPEED_TAX_BASELINE.md:60) and the N_PAD≈16 spill wall. Risk: MEDIUM (replay kernel is real engineering, partially banked; spill-free claim verified by design, not yet at deployed N_PAD=16 e2e). This is the ONLY lever that touches the ACTUAL tax. Lossless: replay re-runs the accepted chain on the same kernel math; committed tokens unchanged.
2. L1 BATCH VERIFY HEAD (N/A — already done). Headroom: ZERO additional (verify head is one batched GEMM since gpu_model_runner.py:4090-4091; the per-row tax was the DRAFTER, already fixed by FIX-1 d407e545). Risk: zero (nothing to change). Keep as a verified PRECONDITION, not a lever.

MATERIAL FAILURE (holds=false) — the lm-head anatomy and bandwidth/tax model are CORRECT and reproduce exactly, but the accept verdict rests on a per-request-vs-aggregate basis error that inverts the conclusion.

WHAT VERIFIES (all source/raw-confirmed):
- Throughput algebra TPS=accept/s_fwd, break-even acc_tree>=(acc_nat+1)*tax-1 is the right model; B=1 + per-request s/fwd ratio avoids the aggregate-deflation pitfall (reference_fr10_speed_measurement_pitfalls); BATCH_INVARIANT=0 confirmed in container_env (not the slow-GEMM artifact). Native s/fwd=29.20597/134=0.21795 (native_probe.json), 64-tok cat9 s/fwd 0.227855/0.227866 + accept 3.1789 (FR13_CHASE_FIXA_BIND.md:87) reproduce. Tax: 64-tok 1.0454x; 11k T1 1.0631x / T2 1.0559x (my recompute over all rows matches MODEL medians).
- lm-head is ONE batched GEMM (gpu_model_runner.py:4090-4091 -> qwen3_next.py:798-802 -> logits_processor.py:96 -> vocab_parallel_embedding.py:69 -> utils.py:98 F.linear), weight bf16 2.5428GB read once; per-row marginal +0.00186ms; 539 rows/+1ms; M=6->9.3254 / M=10->9.3328 / M=15->9.3421 ms all reproduce. The +81.94ms is the DRAFTER gemvx (FR13_B1_SPEED_ATTRIBUTION_BIND.md:16-17, M=1 GEMV, already collapsed by FIX-1 11.10->5.913 gemvx/draft, chain5 1.41->1.051x). L1 correctly a no-op.

WHAT FAILS:
1. ACCEPT GAP NOT CLOSED (the core overstatement). MODEL claims FIX-A closed the -0.43/-0.65 and current gap is ~0 (a draw). REFUTED on the SAME post-FIX-A wf_d8a86320 raw: token-weighted AGGREGATE accept (total_acc/total_drafts) = tree_a 3.1493 vs native_a 3.5765 = -0.427 — i.e. the reshape memory's "-0.43" IS reproduced in current data, it is NOT stale. The near-zero gap only appears on the per-REQUEST-MEDIAN basis (tree 3.5872 vs native 3.5955). Both bases are trajectory-confounded DRAWS (forked at char-80; tree's long requests 985/657 drafts at low accept 2.752/2.717 drive the aggregate down on DIFFERENT token paths than native's). So the accept gap is UNRESOLVED (spans -0.43 aggregate to ~0 median), not closed. MODEL's break-even margins also use tree acc_med=3.652 (T1) where the raw rows give 3.5872 -> true T1 median margin is -0.30, not -0.166/-0.207.
2. L1 NOT unconditionally bit-identical. Greedy accept is an EXACT argmax: rejection_sampler.py:394 target_argmax=target_logits.argmax(dim=-1); kernel line 31 'if draft_token_id != target_argmax_id' rejects. An M-bucket cuBLAS kernel swap (changing M re-selects tile/split-K) can flip a top-2 near-tie argmax -> flip accept -> change the served token. MODEL's 'lossless modulo M-bucket' is honest as a caveat but the unqualified 'batching=lossless' phrasing is too strong. Operationally subsumed only because B=4 byte-exact is already impossible (native self-noise floor bag-TV 0.113, FR13_DIRECTION_AND_NUMBERS:23) -> bar is within-floor, so the gate must be statistical-within-floor, never bit-vs-reference.
3. L2 temp>0/dead-row: savings ~0.006ms and MODEL says don't implement, so moot, but the 'lossless' label needs the within-floor framing (a 'dead' sibling under temp>0 routes via recovered-token resampling on a different node's row, ancestry-gated like greedy; can't pre-prune before parent sample). Net: do not implement.

BOTTOM LINE: lm-head/tax math is sound and the levers ranking (L3+replay >> L1=noop > L2) is correct, but the prompt's premise that the tax-premium is the SOLE remaining gap is wrong — the accept gap is a confounded draw that swings to -0.43 on the token-weighted basis, so even at tax=1.0 the tree's accept lead is not established. A PAIRED teacher-forced same-prefix accept capture (not served trajectories) is required before claiming the tree ties/beats native; the speed-tax break-even is the only clean input the current data provides.
